title: Indian protection qui tam provision (25 U.S.C. 201) enacted
description: Section 201, dating from 1834, lets an informer sue for penalties under five Indian-protection statutes and keep half.
quote: Section 201 dates from 1834 and authorizes qui tam actions for violations of five separate statutes

title: False Claims Act enacted ('Lincoln Law')
description: Congress passed the False Claims Act during the Civil War against fraud by defence contractors; it lets private citizens sue on the government's behalf (qui tam) and share in the recovery.
quote: a federal statute originally enacted in 1863 in response to defense contractor fraud during the American Civil War

title: False Claims Act enacted (Civil War)
description: Act of March 2, 1863 (12 Stat. 696) let any person sue in the name of the United States to recover penalties for frauds on the government; the relator received half of the recovery.
quote: The False Claims Act originated as the Act of March 2, 1863.

title: Original informant-reward law
description: The authority now in section 7623(a) originates in an 1867 law allowing the Treasury to pay sums for detecting and punishing tax violators.
location: printed p. 1 (PDF p. 3), Prior Law and Policy
quote: What is now section 7623(a) ... of the Internal Revenue Code (IRC) has its origins in legislation enacted in 1867.

title: 1943 amendments curtail qui tam
description: After the Attorney General sought repeal, Congress instead cut relator shares (max 25%, or 10% if the government took the case), required relators to hand over their evidence, gave the government 60 days to intervene, and barred suits based on information already in government hands (Pub. L. 78-213, 57 Stat. 608).
quote: The two Houses ultimately reached agreement and passed the compromise as Public Law 78-213.

title: BSA informant rewards enacted
description: 31 U.S.C. 5323 'Rewards for informants' lets Treasury pay up to 25 percent (max $150,000) for information leading to BSA recoveries over $50,000.
quote: (Added Pub. L. 98–473, title II, §901(e), Oct. 12, 1984, 98 Stat. 2135.)

title: False Claims Amendments Act of 1986
description: The 1986 amendments revived qui tam suits: a relator gets 15-25% of the proceeds when the government takes over the case and 25-30% when the relator goes it alone.
quote: receive at least 15 percent but not more than 25 percent of the proceeds of the action or settlement of the claim

title: False Claims Amendments Act of 1986
description: Pub. L. 99-562 revived qui tam: relator shares of 15-25% (government intervenes) or 25-30% (government declines), treble damages, higher penalties, anti-retaliation protection, and a new public-disclosure bar with an original-source exception. Qui tam filings rose from 31 new matters in FY1987 to hundreds a year.
quote: To amend title 31, United States Code, with respect to the fraudulent use of public property or money.

title: Financial Institutions Anti-Fraud Enforcement Act of 1990
description: Lets private persons file confidential declarations of bank-fraud violations with the Attorney General and share in recoveries.

title: 1996 amendments: awards paid from collected proceeds
description: The 1996 amendments added detecting underpayments of tax as a purpose and changed the funding of awards from IRS appropriations to proceeds collected from the taxpayer.
location: printed p. 1 (PDF p. 3), Prior Law and Policy
quote: The 1996 amendments also changed the source of funds from IRS operating funds to proceeds of amounts collected from the taxpayer (other than interest).

title: Taxpayer Bill of Rights 2 rewrites section 7623
description: Pub. L. 104-168 § 1209 adds detecting underpayments as a purpose and removes the appropriations limit; awards are paid from proceeds collected (effective six months after enactment).
quote: 1996—Pub. L. 104–168 substituted ‘‘of underpayments and fraud, etc.’’ for ‘‘and punishment of frauds’’ in section catchline and amended text generally.

title: Second Indian-protection qui tam provision (25 U.S.C. 81) removed
description: The Indian Tribal Economic Development Act (P.L. 106-179) rewrote 25 U.S.C. 81, ending its qui tam action.
quote: This qui tam provision disappeared when the Indian Tribal Economic Development Act rewrote the section, P.L. 106-179, 114 STAT. 46 (2000).

title: Anti-Corruption Act takes effect with rewards for corruption reports
description: The Anti-Corruption Act (Act 6494, enacted 24 Jul 2001) and its decree take effect: people whose corruption reports directly recover public revenue can claim a reward, set at 2-10% of the recovery with a KRW 200 million cap. Run by the Korea Independent Commission Against Corruption, later the ACRC.
quote: 부패행위의 신고자는 이 법에 의한 신고로 인하여 직접적인 공공기관 수입의 회복이나 증대 또는 비용의 절감을 가져온 경우에는 위원회에 보상금의 지급을 신청할 수 있다

title: Sarbanes-Oxley Act section 806: protection for corporate whistleblowers
description: Section 806 created a civil action against retaliation for employees of listed companies who report fraud (18 U.S.C. 1514A). Protection only, no reward.
quote: PROTECTION FOR EMPLOYEES OF PUBLICLY TRADED COMPANIES WHO PROVIDE EVIDENCE OF FRAUD.

title: HCA settlement: largest combined qui tam award at the time ($151.6 million)
description: HCA paid $631 million in civil FCA damages and penalties; whistleblowers received a combined $151,591,500.
quote: the highest combined qui tam award ever paid out by the government.

title: Corruption reward cap raised from KRW 200 million to 2 billion; awards introduced
description: Decree 19238 raises the reward schedule to 4-20% and the cap tenfold, and sets rules for new monetary awards (포상금) of up to KRW 50 million for reports that serve the public interest without a recovery.
quote: 신고보상금 지급한도를 현행 2억원에서 20억원으로 상향조정하고 지급기준도 단계별 보상대상가액에 따라 상향조정함

title: Monetary awards for corruption reports set at up to KRW 50 million, or up to 20% (KRW 200 million) for self-disclosure
description: The amended Anti-Corruption Act decree creates monetary awards (포상금) for reports that bring a public benefit without a revenue recovery: up to KRW 50 million in general, and up to 20% of the amount reported (at most KRW 200 million) for officials who report money or goods they received.
quote: 신고금액 및 신고유형에 따라 차등하여 포상금을 지급할 수 있도록 함

title: Informant claims processing consolidated at Ogden
description: Informant claims operations formerly at five IRS campuses are consolidated in the Ogden Informant Claims Examination unit in FY2006, completed in FY2007.
quote: Informant claims operations formerly assigned to five IRS Campuses were consolidated at the Ogden Informant Claims Examination (ICE) unit in FY 2006.

title: Ghana Whistleblower Act (Act 720) with a Reward Fund
description: Act 720 receives assent; it creates a Whistleblower Reward Fund paying 10% of money recovered (or an amount set by the Attorney-General).
quote: DATE OF ASSENT: 16th October, 2006.

title: Tax Relief and Health Care Act of 2006: mandatory IRS whistleblower awards
description: Section 406 made IRS awards mandatory at 15-30% of collected proceeds for large cases (over $2 million in dispute; individuals with gross income over $200,000) and created the Whistleblower Office.
quote: receive as an award at least 15 percent but not more than 30 percent of the collected proceeds

title: Tax Relief and Health Care Act of 2006 creates section 7623(b)
description: Section 406 of the Act (PL 109-432) re-designates the old discretionary informant-reward law as 7623(a) and adds mandatory awards of 15-30% for cases over $2 million, a Whistleblower Office and Tax Court appeals. Applies to information provided after 19 December 2006.
location: printed p. 2 (PDF p. 4), New Law; Executive Summary
quote: For information provided to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) after December 19, 2006, new section 7623(b) generally requires the IRS to pay awards

title: First Whistleblower Office director appointed
description: The IRS announces Stephen Whitlock as the first Director of the Whistleblower Office.
quote: On February 2, 2007, the IRS announced the appointment of Stephen Whitlock as the first Director of the IRS Whistleblower Office.

title: Notice 2008-4: initial guidance on submitting information
description: IRS Notice 2008-4 and a revised Form 211 give initial guidance on how to submit whistleblower information and the criteria for section 7623(b).
quote: The IRS issued Notice 2008-4 on December 19, 2007 to provide initial guidance on how to submit information to the IRS.

title: Authority to approve 7623(a) awards delegated to the Whistleblower Office Director
description: The IRS delegates approval of discretionary section 7623(a) awards to the Director of the Whistleblower Office.
quote: In 2008, the IRS delegated authority to approve 7623(a) awards to the Director of the Whistleblower Office

title: Notice 2008-4: first guidance on how to file
description: Notice 2008-4 gives initial guidance on submitting information and a revised Form 211; all Forms 211 now go to the Whistleblower Office.
quote: The IRS issued Notice 2008-4 on January 14, 2008.

title: ACRC Act decree replaces the Anti-Corruption Act decree
description: With the Act on the Establishment of the Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission (Act 8878, 29 Feb 2008), the new decree (Presidential Decree 20737) repeals the Anti-Corruption Act decree and moves the reward rules to arts. 71-83 unchanged: rewards 20% down to 4% (annex 1), cap KRW 2 billion, awards up to KRW 50 million (self-disclosure up to 20%, KRW 200 million).
quote: 국민고충처리위원회의 고충민원처리와 국가청렴위원회의 부패방지활동 및 국무총리 행정심판위원회의 기능을 통합하여

title: Court authorises IRS "John Doe" summons on UBS
description: The U.S. District Court in Miami authorised the IRS to serve UBS a John Doe summons for records identifying U.S. taxpayers with concealed UBS accounts in Switzerland (the same month Birkenfeld pleaded guilty). Day not given.
location: paragraph beginning "In June 2008, former UBS private banker Bradley Birkenfeld"
quote: Also, in June 2008, the U.S. District Court in Miami authorized the Internal Revenue Service to serve upon UBS a so-called "John Doe" summons

title: Birkenfeld pleads guilty
description: Former UBS private banker Bradley Birkenfeld pleaded guilty to conspiring to defraud the United States.
quote: On June 19, 2008, Birkenfeld pleaded guilty to conspiring to defraud the United States

title: Whistleblower Executive Board first meets
description: The Whistleblower Executive Board (chaired by the Whistleblower Office Director, with Chief Counsel and operating division executives) held its first meeting; the IRS also awarded a contract for a new case management system that month.
quote: In July 2008, the Whistleblower Executive Board held its first meeting.

title: IRM whistleblower award procedures revised
description: The IRS published revised Internal Revenue Manual provisions on section 7623 after a comprehensive review; the Director of the Whistleblower Office now makes all award determinations, including 7623(a).
quote: published revisions on December 30, 2008

title: New case management system for whistleblower claims
description: The IRS begins recording all new section 7623 claims in a new case management system; legacy data loaded in July 2010.
quote: In January 2009, the IRS began using a new case management system based on commercial-off-the-shelf technology to record all new section 7623 claims.

title: New whistleblower case management system in use
description: The IRS began recording all new section 7623 claims in a new commercial off-the-shelf case management system; by the end of FY2009 all 7623(b) claims had been converted to it.
location: printed p. 4 (PDF p. 5), III.B Case Management Information System
quote: In January 2009, the IRS began using a new case management system based on commercial-off-the-shelf technology to record all new section 7623 claims.

title: UBS deferred prosecution agreement (as reported in the Birkenfeld sentencing release)
description: UBS admitted helping US taxpayers hide accounts from the IRS and agreed to give the US identities and account information of certain US customers.
quote: In February 2009, UBS entered into a deferred prosecution agreement and the bank admitted to helping U.S. taxpayers hide accounts from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS).

title: UBS deferred prosecution agreement: $780 million and client names
description: UBS admitted helping US taxpayers hide accounts, agreed to give the US client identities and to pay $780 million.
quote: Agrees to Identify Customers & Pay $780 Million

title: Fraud Enforcement and Recovery Act of 2009 amends the FCA
description: FERA (Pub. L. 111-21, sec. 4) broadened FCA liability (no need for a claim to be presented directly to a federal officer, materiality defined, conspiracy and reverse false claims expanded) and rewrote the anti-retaliation provision 3730(h).
quote: The amendments of the Fraud Enforcement and Recovery Act of 2009 reinforced the 1986 amendments

title: FERA amends the False Claims Act (Pub. L. 111-21, sec. 4)
description: The Fraud Enforcement and Recovery Act rewrites FCA liability (claims to contractors and grantees covered, "material" and "obligation" defined, reverse false claims), lets the government file its own complaint relating back to the relator's, lets the Attorney General delegate civil investigative demands and share their results with qui tam relators, extends anti-retaliation relief to contractors and agents (reinstatement, two times back pay), and allows service of sealed complaints on state co-plaintiffs. Effective on enactment; the false-record provision applies to claims pending on or after 7 June 2008.
quote: Any information obtained by the Attorney General or a designee of the Attorney General under this section may be shared with any qui tam relator if the Attorney General or designee determine it is necessary as part of any false claims act investigation.

title: Corruption award cap raised from KRW 50 million to KRW 100 million
description: An amendment of the ACRC Act decree (Presidential Decree 21513) raises the cap on monetary awards (포상금) for corruption reports from KRW 50 million to KRW 100 million, for reports received after it takes effect.
quote: 제71조제2항의 개정규정은 부칙 제1조 본문에 따른 제71조제2항의 개정규정의 시행 후 최초로 접수된 신고부터 적용한다

title: Awards wait for the refund-claim period to expire
description: From July 2009 the IRS waits until the taxpayer can no longer claim a refund (generally two years after the last payment) before paying an award, delaying some payments to FY2010-2011.
location: printed p. 8 (PDF p. 9), VI. Whistleblower Awards Paid
quote: beginning in July 2009, the IRS monitors cases both for collection and then for the expiration of the period for filing a claim for refund.

title: UBS agrees to disclose 4,450 more US customers ("John Doe" summons settled)
description: The civil John Doe summons matter was resolved; UBS agreed to produce identities and account information of 4,450 more customers believed to have broken US law.
quote: On Aug. 19, 2009, the civil matter was resolved and UBS agreed to produce the identities and account information of 4,450 additional UBS customers who are believed to have violated United States law.

title: TIGTA: weak control of whistleblower claims, calls for anti-retaliation law
description: TIGTA report 2009-30-114 finds the Whistleblower Office relied on several inaccurate inventory systems and had no timeliness standards; it recommends legislation protecting tax whistleblowers from employer retaliation (enacted in 2019).
quote: Legislation is needed to ensure that informants are protected against retaliation by their employers and to provide specific relief to informants who are retaliated against.

title: Birkenfeld sentenced to 40 months
description: Bradley Birkenfeld was sentenced to 40 months in prison, despite having given the government information on UBS. (Two days earlier UBS agreed to disclose 4,450 more accounts.)
quote: has been sentenced to 40 months incarceration by Judge William J. Zloch in Fort Lauderdale, Fla.

title: SEC inspector general: Madoff warnings ignored
description: The SEC OIG found that between 1992 and 2008 the SEC received six substantive complaints about Madoff, including Harry Markopolos's, but never ran a competent investigation.
quote: the SEC received six 10 substantive complaints that raised significant red flags concerning Madoff’s hedge fund operations

title: Pfizer $2.3 billion settlement, then the largest health care fraud settlement
description: Pfizer paid $2.3 billion; six whistleblowers received more than $102 million.
quote: have agreed to pay $2.3 billion, the largest health care fraud settlement in the history of the Department of Justice

title: GVH press conference on the introduction of the informant reward
description: At the end of March 2010 the Hungarian Competition Authority held a press conference on the introduction of the informant reward, which took effect on 1 April 2010.
quote: március végén az informátori díj bevezetésével kapcsolatban

title: Affordable Care Act rewrites the public-disclosure bar
description: Pub. L. 111-148, sec. 10104(j)(2) replaced the jurisdictional public-disclosure bar with a dismissal rule the government can veto, limited qualifying disclosures to federal sources and the news media, and redefined "original source".
quote: 2010 —Subsec. (e)(4). Pub. L. 111–148 added par. (4) and struck out former par. (4)

title: Hungary introduces informant reward for cartel evidence
description: An amendment to the Hungarian Competition Act (Tpvt.) introduces a reward of 1% of the fine, up to HUF 50 million, for people who provide indispensable written evidence of hard-core cartels.
quote: 2010. április 1-jével lépett hatályba a Tpvt. azon módosítása, amely bevezette az ún. informátori díj intézményét.

title: IRM 25.2.2 revised again (award process guidance)
description: Revised IRM 25.2.2 issued in June 2010 with procedures on the award process as an administrative proceeding, disclosure to whistleblowers, award criteria and application of 7623(b) procedures to 7623(a) cases.
quote: Revised IRM 25.2.2 incorporating these changes was issued in June 2010.

title: IRM 25.2.2 revised: award criteria and whistleblower review of award file
description: Revised Internal Revenue Manual sets procedures for intake and award determinations, including letting 7623(b) whistleblowers comment on preliminary awards; 7623(a) claims filed from 1 July 2010 use the same percentages as 7623(b).
quote: awards paid in section 7623(a) cases submitted on or after July 1, 2010 ... will be determined using the same criteria and percentages that apply to 7623(b) claims.

title: Dodd-Frank Act creates SEC and CFTC whistleblower award programmes
description: Sections 922 (SEC) and 748 (CFTC) require awards of 10-30% of monetary sanctions collected in successful actions.
quote: not less than 10 percent, in total, of what has been collected of the monetary sanctions imposed in the action or related actions

title: Dodd-Frank Act section 748: CFTC whistleblower programme
description: Section 748 added commodity whistleblower incentives and protection to the Commodity Exchange Act.
quote: SEC. 748. COMMODITY WHISTLEBLOWER INCENTIVES AND PROTECTION.

title: Dodd-Frank adds 3-year limit for FCA retaliation claims
description: Pub. L. 111-203, sec. 1079A(c) amended 3730(h) (protection of "associated others" and an explicit 3-year limitations period for retaliation suits).
quote: Dodd-Frank added an explicit 3-year statute of limitations within which a civil action in response to retaliation must be commenced.

title: Dodd-Frank Act creates CFTC whistleblower programme
description: Section 748 added CEA Section 23 (awards of 10-30% of sanctions over $1 million, paid from the new Customer Protection Fund).
quote: Section 748 of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act ... amended the CEA by adding Section 23

title: Dodd-Frank Act creates SEC whistleblower programme
description: Section 922 of the Dodd-Frank Act adds Section 21F to the Exchange Act: awards of 10-30% of sanctions over $1 million, paid from the new Investor Protection Fund.
quote: Section 922 of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act ... adding Section 21F

title: Illinois False Claims Act amended (HB 5951)
description: Governor Quinn signed House Bill 5951, drafted by the Attorney General, amending the Illinois False Claims Act (improved investigative powers, recovery of investigation and litigation costs); effective immediately. Date: the 28 July 2010 release says the Governor signed it 'yesterday'.
quote: The General Assembly unanimously passed the bill and Governor Quinn signed it yesterday. The new law takes effect immediately.

title: Whistleblower Office staff increase to 21 authorised
description: After reviewing intake and expected workload, the IRS authorises raising Whistleblower Office staff from 17 to 21.
quote: the IRS authorized a staff increase to 21 in August 2010.

title: GSK/SB Pharmco $750 million; whistleblower Cheryl Eckard gets about $96 million
description: Named relator Cheryl Eckard received about $96 million from the federal share.
quote: the whistleblower - Cheryl Eckard - will receive approximately $96 million

title: First awards under section 7623(b) paid
description: In FY2011 the IRS paid the first awards under the 2006 law; too few to report separately.
quote: In FY 2011, the Whistleblower Office paid the first claims under the 2006 amendments to section 7623.

title: Patent false-marking qui tam replaced (Leahy-Smith America Invents Act)
description: P.L. 112-29 replaced the Patent Act qui tam provision (35 U.S.C. 292) with a cause of action for victims.
quote: The Leahy-Smith America Invests Act replaced the Patent Act qui tam provision with one that affords victims a cause of action.

title: Proposed regulation on "collected proceeds"
description: The IRS proposes defining collected proceeds for 7623(a) and (b), including reductions of overpayment credit balances and refund-prevention claims.
quote: On January 18, 2011, the IRS issued proposed regulations seeking public comment on a proposal to define the term “collected proceeds”

title: Proposed regulations widen "collected proceeds"
description: IRS proposed regulations (76 Fed. Reg. 2852) defining collected proceeds to include denied refunds and reduced overpayment credits when computing awards.

title: Office of the Whistleblower head appointed
description: The SEC appointed Sean X. McKessy to head the new Office of the Whistleblower.
quote: On February 18, 2011, the Commission announced the appointment of Sean X. McKessy to head the newly-created Office of the Whistleblower

title: Final regulations on contracts with whistleblowers (section 6103(n))
description: Final regulations on contracts for services with whistleblowers, and the disclosure of taxpayer information under them, take effect.
quote: Final regulations governing the use of contracts for services related to the detection of violations of the internal revenue laws or related statutes were published and became ... effective on March 15, 2011.

title: Public Interest Whistleblower Protection Act promulgated
description: The Act on the Protection of Public Interest Whistleblowers was established and promulgated on 29 March 2011; it took effect on 30 September 2011 with its Enforcement Decree.
quote: The Act was established and promulgated on March 29 in 2011

title: First 7623(b) award paid
description: IRS paid the first award under the expanded 7623(b) programme in April 2011, more than four years after the programme began.
quote: the first high-dollar award was paid in April 2011

title: Public hearing on proposed "collected proceeds" regulation
description: Public hearing on the January 2011 proposed regulation defining collected proceeds; final regulation issued 22 Feb 2012.
quote: A public hearing on the proposed regulation was held on May 11, 2011.

title: SEC adopts Regulation 21F
description: Final whistleblower rules adopted 25 May 2011, effective 12 August 2011.
quote: On May 25, 2011, the Commission adopted final Regulation 21F, which became effective on August 12, 2011

title: SEC establishes the Office of the Whistleblower
description: The SEC set up OWB as a separate office within the Division of Enforcement to administer section 21F.
quote: On May 25, 2011, the SEC established OWB as a separate office within the SEC’s Division of Enforcement

title: SEC whistleblower rules (Regulation 21F) published
description: Rules 21F-1 to 21F-17 implementing Section 21F of the Exchange Act published in the Federal Register.
quote: Sections 240.21F-1 through 240.21F-17 appear at 76 FR 34363, June 13, 2011.

title: GAO report on the Whistleblower Office
description: GAO reviews the Whistleblower Office and recommends better case data to track aging claims; the IRS generally agrees.
quote: In August 2011, the Government Accountability Office (GAO) published a report on its review of the Whistleblower Office.

title: SEC whistleblower rules take effect; first 170 Notices of Covered Action
description: Regulation 21F took effect and OWB posted Notices of Covered Action for 170 judgments and orders with sanctions over $1 million.
quote: On August 12, 2011, the Office of the Whistleblower posted Notices of Covered Actions for the 170 applicable enforcement judgments and orders

title: CFTC adopts whistleblower rules (17 CFR Part 165)
description: Final rules implementing CEA Section 23 issued 25 Aug 2011 (76 Fed. Reg. 53172), effective 24 Oct 2011.
quote: The Commission issued final rules implementing Section23 of the CEA on August 25, 2011. These rules became effective on October 24, 2011.

title: CFTC whistleblower rules (Part 165) published
description: Part 165 whistleblower rules implementing Section 23 of the Commodity Exchange Act published in the Federal Register.
quote: 76 FR 53200, Aug. 25, 2011, unless otherwise noted.

title: Public Interest Whistleblower Protection Act takes effect
description: Korea's public-interest whistleblowing law (private-sector violations of health, safety, environment, consumer interests and fair competition) takes effect, with rewards paid by the ACRC.
quote: The ACRC established the Act on the Protection of Public Interest Whistleblowers (effectuated on Sep. 30, 2011

title: Corruption Report Center becomes the Corruption and Public Interest Violation Report Center
description: The ACRC expanded its Corruption Report Center to also receive public-interest violation reports when the new Act took effect.
quote: the Commission has expanded the existing Corruption Report Center to the Corruption and Public Interest Violation Report Center on September 30, 2011

title: PIWPA decree enacted: 169 laws covered, rewards 20% down to 4%, cap KRW 1 billion
description: The first Enforcement Decree of the Public Interest Whistleblower Protection Act (Presidential Decree 23198) takes effect with the Act: it lists 169 covered laws, sets rewards from 20% down to 4% of the recovered amount (annex 2), a KRW 1 billion cap, and relief decisions within 90 days.
quote: 「공익신고자 보호법」이 제정(법률 제10472호, 2011. 3. 29. 제정, 9. 30. 시행)됨에 따라

title: ACRC creates two public-interest whistleblowing divisions
description: The Public Interest Whistleblowing Inspection & Policy Division and the Public Interest Whistleblower Protection Division were set up within the ACRC.
quote: the Public Interest Whistleblowing Inspection & Policy Division and the Public Interest Whistleblower Protection Division were established on October 26, 2011

title: Tax Court proposes rules to protect taxpayer information in whistleblower cases
description: Proposed Tax Court rules to protect taxpayer information, and in some cases the whistleblower's identity, in whistleblower award appeals.
quote: On December 28, 2011, the Tax Court proposed rules to require protection of taxpayer information in Tax Court proceedings

title: Informant Claims Examination unit moves into the Whistleblower Office
description: SB/SE transfers the 13-person ICE unit, which handles discretionary 7623(a) claims, to the Whistleblower Office; office staff reaches 36 by the end of FY2012.
quote: In January 2012, the Small Business/Self-Employed (SB/SE) Division transferred the Informant Claims Examination (ICE) Unit to the Whistleblower Office.

title: Jane Norberg named OWB Deputy Chief
description: The Commission named Jane A. Norberg Deputy Chief of the Office of the Whistleblower.
quote: On January 17, 2012, the Commission named Jane A. Norberg as the Office’s Deputy Chief.

title: Final regulations define "collected proceeds"
description: Final regulations clarify "proceeds of amounts collected" and "collected proceeds", including refund-prevention claims and reductions of overpayment credit balances.
quote: The IRS issued final regulations on February 22, 2012, which clarified the definitions of “proceeds of amounts collected” and “collected proceeds”

title: Interim guidance on award timing and computation (effective 1 Aug 2012)
description: Whistleblower Office interim guidance adds rules on award timing and computation, tax withholding on award payments and administrative proceedings.
quote: On June 7, 2012, the Director of the Whistleblower Office issued interim guidance with an effective date of August 1, 2012.

title: Deputy Commissioner memo sets performance objectives for whistleblower claims
description: Memorandum to division heads on the value of whistleblower information, timely evaluation, debriefings, and performance objectives for evaluations and award determinations.
quote: On June 20, 2012, the Deputy Commissioner for Services and Enforcement issued a memorandum to the Operating Division Commissioners

title: GSK $3 billion, largest health care fraud settlement in US history
description: GSK pleaded guilty and paid $3 billion; four qui tam suits resolved.
quote: The resolution is the largest health care fraud settlement in U.S. history and the largest payment ever by a drug company.

title: First SEC whistleblower award
description: First award under the programme: 30% of sanctions collected, nearly $50,000 paid.
quote: During Fiscal Year 2012, the Commission made its first award under the whistleblower program.

title: IRS pays record US$104 million whistleblower award
description: Largest IRS whistleblower award to that date, confirmed by the IRS under a limited privacy waiver (publicly identified as Bradley Birkenfeld / UBS).
quote: on August 27, 2012, the IRS paid an award of $104 million to a whistleblower.

title: CFTC launches web portal for whistleblower tips
description: The Commission launched its web portal for receiving tips, complaints and referrals (Form TCR) on 10 September 2012.
quote: through the Commission's web portal for receiving tips, complaints and referrals, which was launched on September 10, 2012

title: IRS pays Birkenfeld $104 million
description: Largest IRS whistleblower award to date, paid to a whistleblower who had served prison time in the same affair.
quote: the largest amount ever awarded by the Internal Revenue Service, lawyers for the whistleblower announced Tuesday

title: Proposed comprehensive section 7623 regulations
description: Notice of Proposed Rulemaking: framework for receipt of submissions, evaluation of contribution, and award determination and payment; comments due 19 Feb 2013.

title: SEC Inspector General evaluates the whistleblower programme
description: OIG Report No. 511 found OWB generally prompt, recommended adding performance metrics; found no programme changes necessary.
quote: OIG recommended that the whistleblower program's internal controls be strengthened by adding performance metrics

title: Sequestration cuts whistleblower awards by 8.7%

title: Whistleblower Office notice on sequestration of awards
description: Notice that awards paid from 1 March 2013 are cut by sequestration (8.7 percent).
quote: In April 2013, the Whistleblower Office issued a notice regarding the impact of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985, as amended.

title: Slovak parliament passes fast-track law abolishing the Whistleblower Protection Office
description: The Act on the Office for the Protection of Victims of Crime and Whistleblowers, to replace the Office from 1 January 2026, end its leadership's mandate and allow review and withdrawal of protections, is passed; the president vetoes it on 11 December and parliament overrides the veto on 12 December 2025.
quote: Zákon bol v skrátenom legislatívnom konaní schválený 9. decembra 2025. Nové pravidlá mali začať platiť od 1. januára 2026.

title: Record corruption reward of KRW 1.82 billion
description: Largest reward to one person since 2002, for a report on unlawful free transfer of public land in a redevelopment project.
quote: 역대 최고 보상금 18억 2천만 원을 지급했다고

title: Constitutional Court suspends the law abolishing the Whistleblower Protection Office
description: On a petition by 63 opposition MPs the Constitutional Court suspends the new law; the Office continues unchanged.
quote: Dňa 17. decembra 2025 Ústavný súd SR pozastavil účinnosť schváleného zákona.

title: Treasury opens statutory review of tax and corporate whistleblowing laws
description: Treasury's statutory review under s 1317AK of the Corporations Act consults until 29 July 2026; press reports say the paper discusses financial incentives (paper not read).
quote: Help us identify issues by responding to this consultation by 29 July 2026 .

title: FinCEN: awards only after a final rule
description: FinCEN's programme page says it will begin processing and paying awards once the implementing regulation is final; no award has been paid under the 2021 law.
quote: Once that regulation is finalized, FinCEN will begin processing and paying awards.

title: Record FCA year: over $6.8 billion and 1,297 qui tam suits in FY2025
description: DOJ reported the highest annual FCA settlements and judgments in the Act's history and a record number of qui tam filings (previous record 980 in FY2024).
quote: That amount is the highest in a single year in the history of the False Claims Act.

title: First antitrust whistleblower award ($1 million)
description: $1 million reward for information leading to EBLOCK Corporation's deferred prosecution agreement and $3.28 million fine.
quote: The Antitrust Division today announced its first-ever whistleblower reward

title: European Commission opens infringement over abolition of Slovak Whistleblower Office
description: The Commission opens infringement proceedings over the new law; a EUR 590 million Recovery Plan payment is held back.
quote: Dňa 30. januára 2026 Európska komisia informovala o začatí konania pre porušenie práva EÚ (tzv. infringement)

title: FinCEN bulletin seeks fraud-related tips
description: First whistleblower bulletin, asking for tips on BSA and sanctions violations linked to fraud.
quote: FinCEN Whistleblower Bulletin: Blow the Whistle on Fraud-Related AML and Sanctions Violations

title: Slovak coalition agrees to repeal the law abolishing the Office
description: Prime minister announces the coalition will repeal the new law, citing Recovery Plan payments.
quote: Premiér Robert Fico 4. marca 2026 po rokovaní vlády oznámil, že koalícia sa dohodla na zrušení nového zákona.

title: FinCEN proposes rule to pay whistleblowers
description: FinCEN submits its proposed whistleblower rule to the Federal Register (10-30 percent awards).
quote: Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) submitted to the Federal Register a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM)

title: Whistleblower NPRM published
description: Proposed 31 CFR 1010.930 published; comments due 1 June 2026. No awards are paid until a final rule.
quote: Written comments on this proposed rule must be submitted on or before June 1, 2026.

title: Lithuanian Competition Council offers rewards for evidence in ongoing dairy and coffee-machine investigations
description: The Competition Council invites people with information on its ongoing investigations (a suspected raw-milk purchase price cartel among dairy processors, and suspected resale price fixing of Jura coffee machines by distributor Rickman Trade) to come forward, saying evidence on investigations already under way may earn a reward of up to EUR 100,000.
quote: Individuals who submit evidence related to investigations already being conducted by our institution may also qualify for a reward.

title: SFO Director backs a whistleblower incentivisation scheme
description: SFO Director says he supports an incentivisation scheme for the SFO; over 700 UK nationals provided intelligence to US programmes between 2012 and 2023.
quote: I am a strong advocate for generating human intelligence and I support a whistleblower incentivisation scheme for the SFO.

title: Draft law: 45% tax withheld from Strengthened Reward Scheme payments
description: HMRC publishes draft Finance Bill 2026-27 legislation requiring it to deduct income tax at the additional rate (45%) from rewards under the Strengthened Reward Scheme; effective from Royal Assent.
quote: receive this payment with Income Tax due deducted at source at the additional rate of 45%

title: Independent review recommends SFO whistleblower rewards
description: The Fisher review's second report recommends legislation letting the Serious Fraud Office financially reward whistleblowers, with a consultation on scheme design, plus offences for false reports and harassment.
quote: Make legislative provision for the Serious Fraud Office to financially reward whistleblowers. The Government should launch a consultation to inform the design of a suitable scheme.

title: Flat 30% reward and cap abolition proposed
description: ACRC pre-announces amendments to the enforcement decrees of three laws: a flat 30% of recovered revenue instead of the 4-30% sliding scale, and removal of the 3 billion won cap on corruption and public-funds rewards.
quote: 수입회복액 규모와 상관없이 일괄 30%를 지급하는 방식으로 개편

title: Draft decrees for flat 30% rewards with no cap published for comment
description: The ACRC publishes draft amendments to the enforcement decrees of the ACRC Act, the PIWPA and the Public Funds Recovery Act for 41 days of public comment (14 July to 24 August 2026): rewards at a flat 30% of the recovered amount instead of the 4-30% sliding scale, and no KRW 3 billion cap for corruption and public-funds reports.
quote: 오 늘(14일)부터 8월 24일까지 41일간 입법예고를 진행한다고 밝혔다

title: CWA pilot guidance revised
description: Revised guidance: eligibility under another whistleblower programme no longer automatically bars an award (only duplicate awards are excluded); submissions through a new online intake portal.
quote: being eligible for another whistleblower program no longer automatically renders a whistleblower ineligible for an award

title: New CWA intake portal; over 1,800 tips since launch
description: DOJ fact sheet reports over 1,800 tips in two years and a new intake portal. No award has been announced.
quote: This month, we unveiled a new intake portal to improve the efficiency of the program

title: Eleventh Circuit upholds qui tam under the Appointments Clause (Zafirov)
description: The appeals court vacated the 2024 dismissal, joining other circuits, and remanded for the remaining Take Care and Vesting Clause arguments.
quote: we join our sister circuits that have addressed this issue and hold that the qui tam provisions of the FCA do not violate the Appointments Clause.

title: Eleventh Circuit reverses Zafirov: qui tam does not violate the Appointments Clause
description: Published opinion (Branch, J.): relators do not occupy a continuing position established by law, so they are not officers; joins the 5th, 6th, 9th and 10th Circuits. District court order vacated and case remanded for the Take Care and Vesting Clause arguments, which remain open.
quote: we join our sister circuits that have addressed this issue and hold that the qui tam provisions of the FCA do not violate the Appointments Clause.

title: FinCEN bulletin seeks Iran-related tips
description: Bulletin asking for tips on Iran-related BSA and sanctions violations.
quote: FinCEN Whistleblower Bulletin: Blow the Whistle on Iran-Related Illicit Finance

title: Cabinet approves flat 30% rewards with no cap
description: The Cabinet approves amendments to the three enforcement decrees (ACRC Act, PIWPA, Public Funds Recovery Act); from 29 Sep 2026 rewards are 30% of the recovered amount with no KRW 3 billion cap.
quote: 오늘(22일) 국무회의 의결…오는 9월 29일부터 시행

title: Flat 30% rewards with no cap take effect
description: Cabinet approved the decree amendments on 22 Sep 2026; from 29 Sep 2026 applications get 30% of recovered revenue with no upper limit.
quote: 개정된 시행령은 이달 29일부터 시행되며, 새로운 기준은 시행 이후 신청된 사안부터 적용됩니다.

title: Flat 30% decrees promulgated and in force
description: Presidential Decrees 36730 (ACRC Act), 36731 (PIWPA) and 36732 (Public Funds Recovery Act) are promulgated and take effect the same day; applications filed earlier keep the old schedule.
quote: 이 영은 공포한 날부터 시행한다
